gloss: end of term; end of period

definitions.gloss: end of a school term; end of semester
definitions.explanation: The final portion of an academic term, particularly associated with final exams and grade reports.

definitions.gloss: end of a fiscal or accounting period
definitions.explanation: The closing of a business quarter, fiscal year, or other accounting period, when financial reports are prepared and accounts are settled.

examples.japanese: {期末|きまつ}テストが{近|ちか}い。
examples.english: The end-of-term test is coming up.

examples.japanese: {期末|きまつ}{試験|しけん}に{向|む}けて{勉強|べんきょう}している。
examples.english: I am studying for the final exams.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}から{期末|きまつ}{試験|しけん}が{始|はじ}まるので、{毎日|まいにち}{遅|おそ}くまで{図書館|としょかん}で{勉強|べんきょう}している。
examples.english: Since final exams start next week, I've been studying late at the library every day.

examples.japanese: {期末|きまつ}{決算|けっさん}の{準備|じゅんび}をする。
examples.english: To prepare the end-of-period financial statements.

examples.japanese: {期末|きまつ}の{在庫|ざいこ}{確認|かくにん}を{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: To carry out the end-of-period inventory check.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{期末|きまつ}は{三月|さんがつ}なので、{二月|にがつ}から{経理部|けいりぶ}は{忙|いそが}しくなる。
examples.english: The company's fiscal year ends in March, so the accounting department gets busy starting in February.

notes:
Composed of {期|き} (period/term) and {末|まつ} (end). Used in both academic and business contexts to refer to the end of a defined time period.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {期末|きまつ}{試験|しけん}: final exam
- {期末|きまつ}テスト: end-of-term test
- {期末|きまつ}{決算|けっさん}: end-of-period financial closing
- {期末|きまつ}{報告|ほうこく}: end-of-period report
- {期末|きまつ}{在庫|ざいこ}: end-of-period inventory
- {期末|きまつ}{手当|てあて}: end-of-term allowance

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {学期末|がっきまつ}: end of school term — specifically academic, while {期末|きまつ} covers both academic and business
- {年度末|ねんどまつ}: end of fiscal year — specifically the end of the annual cycle
- {期首|きしゅ}: beginning of a period — the antonym, marking the start of a term or period
- {中間|ちゅうかん}: midterm — the middle of a period, as opposed to the end
